ASSASSINS: THE UNDERWORLD UNCOVERED

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Underworld Hits are happening on YOUR doorstep – we uncover the intricate web behind South Africa’s organized crime networks from debt-collection knockers to illegal gold to drugs and protection

Summary:

The Underworld is alive and well in South Africa. With enemies being taken out regularly. These crime syndicates are interlinked and operating right in suburbia. These criminals are closer than you think.

We uncover the driving forces in the South African Underworld of drugs, gold, money laundering and assasinations.


Further information:
WE ARE NOT GOING TO SET OUT TO SOLVE MARC BATCHELOR’S MURDER OR TO THROW THEORIES AROUND

WE ARE GOING TO INTERVIEW EXPERTS, WHO WILL EXPLAIN THE INTRICACIES BEHIND THE CRIME OPERATIONS IN THE UNDERWORLD.

BATCHELOR’s HIT
Marc Batchelor was gunned down in July in the driveway outside his Olivedale home by two gunmen armed with semi-automatic assault rifles and riding a white motorcycle.

IT APPEARS TO BE HIT – BUT WHY? AND IS THE UNDERWORLD CREEPING INTO SUBURBIA?

BATCHELOR BACKGROUND
He was a debt-collector – but was getting into the business of knocking other knockers (i.e. debt-collectors) and allegedly not making good on the collections he did. He was in partnership with Serb, Ivan Djordjevic, who was killed in Bryanston in April this year. He also teamed up with Gene Kotton – but there appears to have been some bad blood – we have a voice note recording of Batchelor ranting and raving about Kotton. He’s been dabbling into gold dump trading specifically looking at a mine Welkom recently in partnership with Nafis Modack (CPT gangster), Jacques Olkers (JHB Gangster) and Gene Kotton. I’ve heard this from two independent sources.

WHAT’s THE MOTIVE BEHIND BATCHELOR’s MURDER?
So there are five theories at the moment:

1. MODACK – even though Modack came out offering a reward for information on Batchelor’s shooting – some believe it could have been him that ordered the hit. The allegation is that Batchelor owed Modack money in the gold dump deal. Also it’s alleged that Batchelor was using Modack’s name in his debt-collection but might have thrown it around with the wrong crowd.
2. GENE KOTTON – bad blood between two, Batchelor was threatening to out Kotton to Modack about money that was due to him, but not paid over.
3. THE TON OF COCAINE – as a known drug user – it is highly unlikely that Batchelor would have been trusted with a drug deal of that magnitude. But it is alleged that he was involved in the theft of the ton cocaine along with Ivan Djordjevic who was killed in Sept 2018.
4. ISRAELI BUSINESSMAN (???) The Sunday Times suggested that Batchelor got on the wrong side of an Israeli Businessman after failing to pay over a R3.5 million collection he made on the businessman’s behalf earlier in July.
5. MICKEY SCHULTZ – apparently this crowd was not happy with the way Batchelor did collections and claimed he was giving the industry a bad name.

EXPERTS
We speak to underworld experts like journalist and author Mandy Weiner, PI Chad Thomas who’s worked on these case directly, Mark Shaw head of Criminology at UCT, author of Hitmen for Hire and part of the Assassination Witness Research Project. They are able to paint a picture of the how the different spheres are linked and how the territories are becoming murky.

Assassination Witness has done extensive research in SA over the last 20 years documenting the different motives behind hits. Research last published in 2017 put organized crime hits at 23% of all assassination in the country.

According to experts there are three key low intensity underworlds on the go in South Africa:
1. CAPE TOWN – the enforcers for the club doors – bouncers and “protection services” are not just the gatekeepers, they run the drug scene so play a crucial role in underworld operations. HITS – Jurie the Russian, Cyril Beeka, Adv Mahlik
2. THE SERBS – they are responsible for cocaine distribution – their king pin was Miso Mihaljevic’s who died in 2013, his son Djordje was taken out in a hit in Bedfordview in 2018 when he was on his way home in the north of Johannesburg - he was shot by two gunmen on a motorcycle. The Serb leadership is in turmoil
3. THE JHB UNDERWORLD – since Radovan Krejcir’s incarseration there has been a gap for the top spot of JHB organised crime with people like Mickey Schultz, Marc Batchelor and Gene Kotton all vying to be the boss.

From shootings at KFC drive throughs, to hits in the parking lots of Bryanston residential complexes to legs being broken with hammers – these hits are brutal.

There have been 20 years of hits snowballing in South Africa coming closer to ordinary citizen and the fear is that we could see some serious collateral damage in the near future.

HISTORY OF MOTORCYCLE ASSASSAINATIONS
This modus operandi dates back to 1980s in Colombia where it was predominantly used by Pablo Escobar and the Godmother of Cocaine, Griselda Blanco both used this method widely to eliminate enemies. To this day, two men riding on a motorcycle is banned in parts of Columbia. It was used for the first time in SA in the early 2000’s when Israeli Gangster Lior Saat was shot in the butt when two men on a motorcycle shot at the prison vehicle he was being transported in to court and has since been used repeatedly – most recently in Mihaljevic and Batchelor’s murders.


INTERVIEWS AROUND BATCHELOR SHOOTING
- I suggest first prize is interviewing the gardener – then we don’t need Warren Batchelor – he has said that they were estranged for the last two years and have recently started chatting but had yet to meet.

INTERVIEWS ABOUT THE UNDERWORLD
- NAFIS MODACK

FOOTAGE
There are some clips of recent hits, lots of photos from crime scenes and pics of the people taken out.

We need a day’s filming in Cape Town to interview Nafis Modack and Mark Shaw.

There are a lot of layers and fascinating material – this is definitely 12 minutes worth – I will be shooting three days and hiring actors to do the re-enactments.

SHOOT
TUESDAY & WEDNESDAY & THURSDAY – 20. 21. 22 of Augst
EDIT
FOLLOWING WEEK WITH FLORIS (he’s already booked for Kate….)

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: From to drugs to extortion, the stakes are high in the world of organized crime pumping hundreds of millions of Rands in illegal business.

LINK: The Underworld is alive and well. With enemies being taken out all over the country – more often than you’d like think. This is not movie scenes I’m talking about – these hits are happening on the streets in your suburbs.

VO: Former Bafana Bafana Soccer star Marc Batchelor was gunned down in July outside his Olivedale home in Joburg.

This is exclusive CCTV footage of the shooting – watch as Batchelor’s car stops to turn into the drive way, when a motorbike with two men approaches from behind, the gunman fired several shots with a semi-automatic assault rifle and then sped off.

He died at the scene. While the motives are still unclear and no arrests have been made – it appears to have been a hit.

MANDY: //The truth is the underworld is all around us – all the time

VO: It’s only with high-profile assassinations that the public gets a glimpse into the sinister underworld. Journalist & author Mandy Weiner has written extensively on criminal networks.
MANDY WIDE
MANDY: Life has become so cheap in this country and it’s so easy to find somebody that will be paid to carry out an execution for you.

VO: Since the early 2000’s there’s been a string of mafia style hits from Brett Kebble to Lolly Jackson to Advocate Pete Mihalik who represented Cape Town’s key underworld figures he was gunned down at his children’s school.

Ivan Djordjevic who was alleged link to a Serbian organised crime ring was killed by gun-wielding hitmen at a residential complex in Bryanstan.

And tobacco baron Simon Rudland survived an attempted assissination just weeks ago – he was shot three times in a drive-by hit.

These shootings appear to have been hired hits.

MARK: // we are talking about people practicing violence that's subject to the whims of a broader economy.

VO: Mark Shaw, from the Global Initiative against Transnational Organised Crime in Geneva says, there are different levels of hitmen operating in South African criminal networks.

MARK: // at the lowest level are people with very few skills maybe not any experience at all who advertise their experience; at a middle level are hit men who have acquired a reasonable degree of experience largely in the taxi and gang environment // and then a third category of very specialized people maybe being brought in external externally to the country or linked to particular groups.

VO: Most of these specialist assassins hail from Serbia believes Private Investigator Chad Thomas who has worked on cases linked to the underworld.

CHAD: // they are imported specifically for that job // that is hwat they are known for within in Eastern Europe – and that particular group of eastern eurpoeans is very prevalent in SA at the moment – they are prevalent within the international drug scene – they are prevalent in the international assassination scene.

VO: The majority of hitmen in South Africa are locals. This is an ex-mid-level hitman from the Western Cape. He claims to have killed at least 25 people in his career.

DEVI – did you find that as you did it you became braver and braver
DON: it becomes like an addiction. INT1 M6 // that’s what everbody expects of you, //INT2 M1 // this is your job – like a soccer player that goes to practice to play for money – this is work. INT2 M4 // that’s the way you make your money

VO: And there’s money to made Shaw’s research revealed.

MARK: // it really depends on the difficulty. So for a relatively easy 10 20 30 thousand but up into the hundred thousands. And remember people think of these things as an investment. And // hope to get some personal gain some political gain. // or some economic gain

LINK: From swanky night clubs to gold mines to the streets, the underworld is at war to control valuable commodities whether its drugs, gold or dirty money.

MANDY: // sometimes it is about its market share – so its about tobacco – it’s about a share of the market, if you look at the nightclub security industry – he who controls the doors, controls the drug trade

CHAD: // SA being a trasn shipment hub, has become an international focus of organised crime // INT1 M12 // Drugs are huge, // human trafficking in and out of SA// using different commidites to swop for drugs, perlemoen is massive// what do they swop out for that ivory, what do they swop out for that rhino horn – so those things paly a hugely in the control of resources.

VO: And the motives for these types of hits are diverse.

CHAD: // you’ve got turf wars going on, you’ve got grudge fights going on, you’ve got people that are involved with one group and are not paying their debt to that group so they are getting taken out –INT2 M2 // The message is clear – I don’t think there is any threats any more. I think there is just hits.

VO: Revenge is also a big driving force.

MANDY: The other problem we are seeing is tat for tat – where somebody will kill somebody in a rival gang and they will then return that and kill somebody in response as revenge and that is what makes it so costly – because that cycle continues in perpetuity.

VO: The ex-hitman’s first murder was a revenge kill when he was just 13 years old.

DON: // one of my friend got killed – so it was like revenge – did what I had to do

VO: A trend that is prominent, even up the ranks - in April, an alleged gang boss, was gunned down in a brazen hit at a petrol station in Cape Town in a suspected revenge attack for the death of a rival gang leader.

Ebrahiem “Hiema” Ismail, was shot 17 times in the head and the chest.

The repurcussions of Cape Gangs are not limited to the Western Cape – it will be felt far and wide believes Thomas.

CHAD: // it looks very disorganised, one doesn’t understand that those are just footsoldiers – there is a whole hierarchy – so the person sitting on top is not somebody sitting in that particular township – somebody sitting in Clifton, maybe sitting in bryanston in

MANDY: // the days of somebody only being powerful in one suburb in cppt – are over – now they are influential in JHB, in DBN and they can call the shots//, the country is small, the world is small. // we see that relationship between organised crime and business, and politics and how influential they can be across the country

LINK: These criminal syndicates don’t operate in isolated bubbles – their territories overlap, their worlds collide in a fight to control illegal networks – their battles have been moving out of the shadows.

VO: Increasingly putting innocent bystanders in the line of fire.

MANDY: but if you look at what his happening in gangland shootings – extremely concering //. collateral damage is an issue – the more professional the hit = the less the collateral damage

VO: Getting close to the target is the goal – the ex-hitman we spoke to says he was taught this basic MO by fellow gangsters.

DON: // the person will walk up to the bottle, put the gun agains the bottle and shoot the bottle – and say that’s the way you must walk up to them – how to get close to the person

CHAD: drive by shootings are not as accurate and sometimes it’s just to send a message, // when people are serious about killing somebody we see the motorbikes coming out.

VO: This modus operandi dates back to 1980s in Colombia where druglords like Pablo Escobar used this method widely to eliminate enemies.

CHAD: //in fact they used it so successfully that riding pillion between certain hours of the day in medilline in Collumbia became illegal because so many people were killed by people riding on motorbikes.

VO: An MO that has been used at least 5 times in South Africa to execute high-profile people.

Preliminary data shows that in 2018 there were just over 200 hits in the country –with organized crime making up about 23%.

MARK: // in the South African context this kind of targeted murder is part of our overall murder rate. // we need to understand that violence is used //as a means to regulate criminal markets.

VO: Criminal markets that will continue to thrive while the criminal justice remains weak.

MANDY: // while we might see the actual shooters being arrested on occasion it is very rare that we see the person who has ordered the hit being arrested, // INT1 M23 MIDDLE// we don’t have the capacity to deal with organised crime there are no consequences for these crimes that are being committed – that is why there is this sense of invincibility

DON: You start to believe nobody can touch me, I am untouchable

VO: The harsh reality though, is in these circles, deadmen tell no tales explains Shaw.

MARK: they are very very vulnerable to being killed themselves so they because they get to know too much they become a power in their own right. And so they their lives and the work they conduct is is relatively fragile.

DON: // the further you go in to this, the more you start to see and know // you can become like a problem for them in the long run // where the hunter becomes the hunter.

DEVI: No honor amongst thieves
MARK: // there's competition between between between people in the illicit economy because of course there's a deficit of trust. And so the symbolism of of hits and the use of hits as a form of regulatory violence is often a mechanism to replace trust.
 
PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: Underworld Hits on YOUR doorstep – as the bodies pile up, we uncover the intricate web behind South Africa’s organized crime networks from debt-collection to drugs and human trafficking;.

PROMO 2
VO: We uncover the driving forces behind South Africa’s Underworld hits as rival criminal networks clash in the fight to get control of illicit operations from drugs to gold and extortion.

PROMO 3
VO: The Underworld is creeping out of the shadows and into the suburbs with assassination style hits happening out in plane sight as criminal networks collide in their battle to control illicit commodities.

VO: The majority of hitmen in South Africa are locals. This is an ex-mid-level hitman from the Western Cape. He claims to have killed at least 25 people in his career. DEVI – did you find that as you did it you became braver and braver DON: it becomes like an addiction. INT1 M6 // that’s what everbody expects of you, //INT2 M1 // this is your job – like a soccer player that goes to practice to play for money – this is work. INT2 M4 // that’s the way you make your money VO: And there’s money to made Shaw’s research revealed. MARK: // it really depends on the difficulty. So for a relatively easy 10 20 30 thousand but up into the hundred thousands. And remember people think of these things as an investment. And // hope to get some personal gain some political gain. // or some economic gain LINK: From swanky night clubs to gold mines to the streets, the underworld is at war to control valuable commodities whether its drugs, gold or dirty money. MANDY: // sometimes it is about its market share – so its about tobacco – it’s about a share of the market, if you look at the nightclub security industry – he who controls the doors, controls the drug trade CHAD: // SA being a trasn shipment hub, has become an international focus of organised crime // INT1 M12 // Drugs are huge, // human trafficking in and out of SA// using different commidites to swop for drugs, perlemoen is massive// what do they swop out for that ivory, what do they swop out for that rhino horn – so those things paly a hugely in the control of resources. VO: And the motives for these types of hits are diverse. CHAD: // you’ve got turf wars going on, you’ve got grudge fights going on, you’ve got people that are involved with one group and are not paying their debt to that group so they are getting taken out –INT2 M2 // The message is clear – I don’t think there is any threats any more. I think there is just hits. VO: Revenge is also a big driving force. MANDY: The other problem we are seeing is tat for tat – where somebody will kill somebody in a rival gang and they will then return that and kill somebody in response as revenge and that is what makes it so costly – because that cycle continues in perpetuity. VO: The ex-hitman’s first murder was a revenge kill when he was just 13 years old. DON: // one of my friend got killed – so it was like revenge – did what I had to do VO: A trend that is prominent, even up the ranks - in April, an alleged gang boss, was gunned down in a brazen hit at a petrol station in Cape Town in a suspected revenge attack for the death of a rival gang leader. Ebrahiem “Hiema” Ismail, was shot 17 times in the head and the chest. The repurcussions of Cape Gangs are not limited to the Western Cape – it will be felt far and wide believes Thomas. CHAD: // it looks very disorganised, one doesn’t understand that those are just footsoldiers – there is a whole hierarchy – so the person sitting on top is not somebody sitting in that particular township – somebody sitting in Clifton, maybe sitting in bryanston in MANDY: // the days of somebody only being powerful in one suburb in cppt – are over – now they are influential in JHB, in DBN and they can call the shots//, the country is small, the world is small. // we see that relationship between organised crime and business, and politics and how influential they can be across the country LINK: These criminal syndicates don’t operate in isolated bubbles – their territories overlap, their worlds collide in a fight to control illegal networks – their battles have been moving out of the shadows. VO: Increasingly putting innocent bystanders in the line of fire. MANDY: but if you look at what his happening in gangland shootings – extremely concering //. collateral damage is an issue – the more professional the hit = the less the collateral damage VO: Getting close to the target is the goal – the ex-hitman we spoke to says he was taught this basic MO by fellow gangsters. DON: // the person will walk up to the bottle, put the gun agains the bottle and shoot the bottle – and say that’s the way you must walk up to them – how to get close to the person CHAD: drive by shootings are not as accurate and sometimes it’s just to send a message, // when people are serious about killing somebody we see the motorbikes coming out. VO: This modus operandi dates back to 1980s in Colombia where druglords like Pablo Escobar used this method widely to eliminate enemies. CHAD: //in fact they used it so successfully that riding pillion between certain hours of the day in medilline in Collumbia became illegal because so many people were killed by people riding on motorbikes. VO: An MO that has been used at least 5 times in South Africa to execute high-profile people. Preliminary data shows that in 2018 there were just over 200 hits in the country –with organized crime making up about 23%. MARK: // in the South African context this kind of targeted murder is part of our overall murder rate. // we need to understand that violence is used //as a means to regulate criminal markets. VO: Criminal markets that will continue to thrive while the criminal justice remains weak. MANDY: // while we might see the actual shooters being arrested on occasion it is very rare that we see the person who has ordered the hit being arrested, // INT1 M23 MIDDLE// we don’t have the capacity to deal with organised crime there are no consequences for these crimes that are being committed – that is why there is this sense of invincibility DON: You start to believe nobody can touch me, I am untouchable VO: The harsh reality though, is in these circles, deadmen tell no tales explains Shaw. MARK: they are very very vulnerable to being killed themselves so they because they get to know too much they become a power in their own right. And so they their lives and the work they conduct is is relatively fragile. DON: // the further you go in to this, the more you start to see and know // you can become like a problem for them in the long run // where the hunter becomes the hunter. DEVI: No honor amongst thieves MARK: // there's competition between between between people in the illicit economy because of course there's a deficit of trust. And so the symbolism of of hits and the use of hits as a form of regulatory violence is often a mechanism to replace trust. metadata.Summary: The Underworld is alive and well in South Africa. With enemies being taken out regularly. These crime syndicates are interlinked and operating right in suburbia. These criminals are closer than you think. We uncover the driving forces in the South African Underworld of drugs, gold, money laundering and assasinations.
metadata.Further information: WE ARE NOT GOING TO SET OUT TO SOLVE MARC BATCHELOR’S MURDER OR TO THROW THEORIES AROUND WE ARE GOING TO INTERVIEW EXPERTS, WHO WILL EXPLAIN THE INTRICACIES BEHIND THE CRIME OPERATIONS IN THE UNDERWORLD. BATCHELOR’s HIT Marc Batchelor was gunned down in July in the driveway outside his Olivedale home by two gunmen armed with semi-automatic assault rifles and riding a white motorcycle. IT APPEARS TO BE HIT – BUT WHY? AND IS THE UNDERWORLD CREEPING INTO SUBURBIA? BATCHELOR BACKGROUND He was a debt-collector – but was getting into the business of knocking other knockers (i.e. debt-collectors) and allegedly not making good on the collections he did. He was in partnership with Serb, Ivan Djordjevic, who was killed in Bryanston in April this year. He also teamed up with Gene Kotton – but there appears to have been some bad blood – we have a voice note recording of Batchelor ranting and raving about Kotton. He’s been dabbling into gold dump trading specifically looking at a mine Welkom recently in partnership with Nafis Modack (CPT gangster), Jacques Olkers (JHB Gangster) and Gene Kotton. I’ve heard this from two independent sources. WHAT’s THE MOTIVE BEHIND BATCHELOR’s MURDER? So there are five theories at the moment: 1. MODACK – even though Modack came out offering a reward for information on Batchelor’s shooting – some believe it could have been him that ordered the hit. The allegation is that Batchelor owed Modack money in the gold dump deal. Also it’s alleged that Batchelor was using Modack’s name in his debt-collection but might have thrown it around with the wrong crowd. 2. GENE KOTTON – bad blood between two, Batchelor was threatening to out Kotton to Modack about money that was due to him, but not paid over. 3. THE TON OF COCAINE – as a known drug user – it is highly unlikely that Batchelor would have been trusted with a drug deal of that magnitude. But it is alleged that he was involved in the theft of the ton cocaine along with Ivan Djordjevic who was killed in Sept 2018. 4. ISRAELI BUSINESSMAN (???) The Sunday Times suggested that Batchelor got on the wrong side of an Israeli Businessman after failing to pay over a R3.5 million collection he made on the businessman’s behalf earlier in July. 5. MICKEY SCHULTZ – apparently this crowd was not happy with the way Batchelor did collections and claimed he was giving the industry a bad name. EXPERTS We speak to underworld experts like journalist and author Mandy Weiner, PI Chad Thomas who’s worked on these case directly, Mark Shaw head of Criminology at UCT, author of Hitmen for Hire and part of the Assassination Witness Research Project. They are able to paint a picture of the how the different spheres are linked and how the territories are becoming murky. Assassination Witness has done extensive research in SA over the last 20 years documenting the different motives behind hits. Research last published in 2017 put organized crime hits at 23% of all assassination in the country. According to experts there are three key low intensity underworlds on the go in South Africa: 1. CAPE TOWN – the enforcers for the club doors – bouncers and “protection services” are not just the gatekeepers, they run the drug scene so play a crucial role in underworld operations. HITS – Jurie the Russian, Cyril Beeka, Adv Mahlik 2. THE SERBS – they are responsible for cocaine distribution – their king pin was Miso Mihaljevic’s who died in 2013, his son Djordje was taken out in a hit in Bedfordview in 2018 when he was on his way home in the north of Johannesburg - he was shot by two gunmen on a motorcycle. The Serb leadership is in turmoil 3. THE JHB UNDERWORLD – since Radovan Krejcir’s incarseration there has been a gap for the top spot of JHB organised crime with people like Mickey Schultz, Marc Batchelor and Gene Kotton all vying to be the boss. From shootings at KFC drive throughs, to hits in the parking lots of Bryanston residential complexes to legs being broken with hammers – these hits are brutal. There have been 20 years of hits snowballing in South Africa coming closer to ordinary citizen and the fear is that we could see some serious collateral damage in the near future. HISTORY OF MOTORCYCLE ASSASSAINATIONS This modus operandi dates back to 1980s in Colombia where it was predominantly used by Pablo Escobar and the Godmother of Cocaine, Griselda Blanco both used this method widely to eliminate enemies. To this day, two men riding on a motorcycle is banned in parts of Columbia. It was used for the first time in SA in the early 2000’s when Israeli Gangster Lior Saat was shot in the butt when two men on a motorcycle shot at the prison vehicle he was being transported in to court and has since been used repeatedly – most recently in Mihaljevic and Batchelor’s murders. INTERVIEWS AROUND BATCHELOR SHOOTING - I suggest first prize is interviewing the gardener – then we don’t need Warren Batchelor – he has said that they were estranged for the last two years and have recently started chatting but had yet to meet. INTERVIEWS ABOUT THE UNDERWORLD - NAFIS MODACK FOOTAGE There are some clips of recent hits, lots of photos from crime scenes and pics of the people taken out. We need a day’s filming in Cape Town to interview Nafis Modack and Mark Shaw. There are a lot of layers and fascinating material – this is definitely 12 minutes worth – I will be shooting three days and hiring actors to do the re-enactments. SHOOT TUESDAY & WEDNESDAY & THURSDAY – 20. 21. 22 of Augst EDIT FOLLOWING WEEK WITH FLORIS (he’s already booked for Kate….)
